Who killed Agatha?

Derivation found by ground unit propagation. This reader uses the reduced checked atom catalogue.

Read the input premises
  1. \(\exists x{:}\mathrm{U}\;\bigl(\mathrm{lives}\left(x\right) \land \mathrm{killed}\left(x, \mathrm{agatha}\right)\bigr)\)
  2. \(\mathrm{lives}\left(\mathrm{agatha}\right)\)
  3. \(\mathrm{lives}\left(\mathrm{butler}\right)\)
  4. \(\mathrm{lives}\left(\mathrm{charles}\right)\)
  5. \(\forall x{:}\mathrm{U}\;\bigl(\mathrm{lives}\left(x\right) \to \bigl(x=\mathrm{agatha} \lor \bigl(x=\mathrm{butler} \lor x=\mathrm{charles}\bigr)\bigr)\bigr)\)
  6. \(\forall x{:}\mathrm{U}\;\forall y{:}\mathrm{U}\;\bigl(\mathrm{killed}\left(x, y\right) \to \mathrm{hates}\left(x, y\right)\bigr)\)
  7. \(\forall x{:}\mathrm{U}\;\forall y{:}\mathrm{U}\;\bigl(\mathrm{killed}\left(x, y\right) \to \neg\bigl(\mathrm{richer}\left(x, y\right)\bigr)\bigr)\)
  8. \(\forall x{:}\mathrm{U}\;\bigl(\mathrm{hates}\left(\mathrm{agatha}, x\right) \to \neg\bigl(\mathrm{hates}\left(\mathrm{charles}, x\right)\bigr)\bigr)\)
  9. \(\forall x{:}\mathrm{U}\;\bigl(x\ne \mathrm{butler} \to \mathrm{hates}\left(\mathrm{agatha}, x\right)\bigr)\)
  10. \(\forall x{:}\mathrm{U}\;\bigl(\neg\bigl(\mathrm{richer}\left(x, \mathrm{agatha}\right)\bigr) \to \mathrm{hates}\left(\mathrm{butler}, x\right)\bigr)\)
  11. \(\forall x{:}\mathrm{U}\;\bigl(\mathrm{hates}\left(\mathrm{agatha}, x\right) \to \mathrm{hates}\left(\mathrm{butler}, x\right)\bigr)\)
  12. \(\forall x{:}\mathrm{U}\;\exists y{:}\mathrm{U}\;\neg\bigl(\mathrm{hates}\left(x, y\right)\bigr)\)
  13. \(\mathrm{agatha}\ne \mathrm{butler}\)

Conclusion

\(\mathrm{killed}\left(\mathrm{agatha}, \mathrm{agatha}\right)\)

A line through two distinct points is unique

Derivation found by marked serial clause-block search. This reader uses the reduced checked atom catalogue.

Read the input premises
  1. \(\forall a{:}\mathrm{Point}\;\forall b{:}\mathrm{Point}\;\forall l{:}\mathrm{Line}\;\forall m{:}\mathrm{Line}\;\bigl(\bigl(a\ne b \land \bigl(I\left(a, l\right) \land \bigl(I\left(b, l\right) \land \bigl(I\left(a, m\right) \land I\left(b, m\right)\bigr)\bigr)\bigr)\bigr) \to l=m\bigr)\)
  2. \(a\ne b\)
  3. \(I\left(a, \ell\right)\)
  4. \(I\left(b, \ell\right)\)

Conclusion

\(\forall m{:}\mathrm{Line}\;\bigl(\bigl(I\left(a, m\right) \land I\left(b, m\right)\bigr) \to \ell=m\bigr)\)

A seven-cycle has no two-coloring

The learned schedule selected two checked lemma outputs per receptor. Its derivation was expanded to source clauses and checked.

Read the input premises
  1. \(\bigl(\mathrm{claim}\left(a\right) \lor \bigl(\mathrm{color0}\left(a\right) \lor \mathrm{color1}\left(a\right)\bigr)\bigr)\)
  2. \(\bigl(\mathrm{claim}\left(a\right) \lor \bigl(\mathrm{color1}\left(a\right) \lor \mathrm{color2}\left(a\right)\bigr)\bigr)\)
  3. \(\bigl(\mathrm{claim}\left(a\right) \lor \bigl(\mathrm{color2}\left(a\right) \lor \mathrm{color3}\left(a\right)\bigr)\bigr)\)
  4. \(\bigl(\mathrm{claim}\left(a\right) \lor \bigl(\mathrm{color3}\left(a\right) \lor \mathrm{color4}\left(a\right)\bigr)\bigr)\)
  5. \(\bigl(\mathrm{claim}\left(a\right) \lor \bigl(\mathrm{color4}\left(a\right) \lor \mathrm{color5}\left(a\right)\bigr)\bigr)\)
  6. \(\bigl(\mathrm{claim}\left(a\right) \lor \bigl(\mathrm{color5}\left(a\right) \lor \mathrm{color6}\left(a\right)\bigr)\bigr)\)
  7. \(\bigl(\mathrm{claim}\left(a\right) \lor \bigl(\mathrm{color6}\left(a\right) \lor \mathrm{color0}\left(a\right)\bigr)\bigr)\)
  8. \(\bigl(\mathrm{claim}\left(a\right) \lor \bigl(\neg\bigl(\mathrm{color0}\left(a\right)\bigr) \lor \neg\bigl(\mathrm{color1}\left(a\right)\bigr)\bigr)\bigr)\)

Learn which checked lemma batches to admit

When a source clause reaches the frontier, its receptors offer checked lemma outputs. A batch takes up to zero, two, eight, thirty-two or all distinct candidates. Every arm ranks candidates by width, contact with settled clauses and recipe length. The shuffled arm samples the same quota before restoring rank order.

Training used 11 separate synthetic cases and 30 paired anchor contexts. In each context, one batch action changed and the other actions followed the reference schedule. The policy gradient used the measured reward of all five rollouts. The frozen policy selected two at all 93 held-out windows it reached. It ties the fixed-two schedule.

The training score \(W=P+\lceil S/4\rceil+4A+R\) counts resolution pair attempts, subset probes, admitted claims and final replay steps respectively. This is an experimental weighting. The component counts and one-time library validation appear separately.

Prune failures and expand only the lemmas used

Two complementary contacts forbid every one-pivot join of a clause pair. A stronger clause already in the agenda can subsume a proposed resolvent. The checks replay these two failure marks from exact literal sets. Here is the earlier four-pigeon pilot with the same composed library.

Learn cuts on the statement atoms

The four-hole cases offered no placements with one extra literal per receptor. Allowing two extras created checked offers, while each clause saturation schedule still reached the common limit. Ground Glucose saw the same input and the certified output clauses.

The atom search branches on truth values for ground statement atoms. A propagation failure traces back to a clause over the decisions. The search can jump past irrelevant decisions, and an independent pass replays every learned cut. One cut from the five-pigeon search appears below.

Give the checker a smaller atom catalogue

The certificate includes only atoms used by the found proof. Every literal in a selected ground source instance still needs a matching atom, so deleting a literal cannot make that premise easier to admit. The attack changed an original premise to its truncated version. Both attacks were rejected.

StatementFull atomsReduced atomsFull gatesReduced gatesOmission attack
Agatha2641848295167686REJECTED
Hilbert incidence126146309668REJECTED

Both full circuits accept their respective derivations. Ground unit propagation found the quantified Agatha proof at term depth one. The earlier marked serial search found Hilbert incidence uniqueness. Vampire guide example
